title: Conditions and adab of the murid
summary: Who can give bai'at, how to choose a murshid, how to sit in his company, what to do after a slip, and how Hazrat speaks of khilafat.

blocks.p: Hazrat reads that some say the murid should be an adult, and some that he should have understanding and insight: able to tell good from bad. Sometimes bai'at is taken even from small children for blessing; this is called bai'at-e-barakat. For women, bai'at by word of mouth is enough, and Hazrat reads that a woman does not need to unveil before the shaykh, however old he may be.

blocks.h: Look first, then give your hand

blocks.p: Hazrat reads that the shaykh should be able to fulfil the aim of discipleship, should know the verses of the Qur'an's commands and the necessary matters of hadith and fiqh, and should have been blessed by the company of an experienced personality. Permission to give khilafat, he says, comes from above, through the chain of murshids.

blocks.q: Some elders have given this mark of a good murshid: in whose company all whisperings and idle thoughts stop, and a person's mind becomes bound to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. Look first and understand, then give your hand. Otherwise regret follows.
When I speak, keep looking into my eyes. The states that come out of my eyes come into your eyes too. That is why you should keep your eyes open and keep looking at the murshid.

blocks.p: The Companions used to keep looking at the Prophet ﷺ, Hazrat says, and they also lowered their gaze out of respect.

blocks.q: If someone makes a mistake after giving bai'at, he should repent and say: Astaghfirullah al-'Azeem alladhi la ilaha illa Huwa al-Hayy al-Qayyum wa atubu ilayh. Repentance never goes to waste.

blocks.p: Hazrat also tells of a Companion whom the Prophet ﷺ told to give bai'at again, though he had already given it. 'Once you have given bai'at, renew it,' Hazrat says. 'That is what I do.'

Khilafat, Hazrat says, comes from above. A murid may wonder whether he is worthy, but he should not ask; he should stay silent. Khilafat is the confirmation that a murid has become worthy, like a certificate given after study.

blocks.q: Neither a merely formal discipleship is of any use, nor a merely formal khilafat.
That is why I keep saying: read this book. It teaches not only the murid, but the shaykh too.

blocks.note: Hazrat also says he makes no one a murid without permission from Sarkar, and sometimes sends a person back (Nizam-ul-Amal part 3, 27:44). The recording does not make clear whether Sarkar here means the Prophet ﷺ or his shaykh: ask your teacher.
